articles.title: LIV Golf’s attempted relaunch collapses after new lead investor withdraws, reports say
articles.summary: BC Partners reportedly walks away after player exodus. LIV set to appear at bankruptcy hearing on Thursday. The rebel LIV Golf tour’s attempt to relaunch itself after filing for bankruptcy has collapsed following the withdrawal of the new lead investor BC Partners, according to reports on…
body: The private capital firm made the decision to walk away after struggling to convince several star players to commit fully to the league going forward, the Financial Times and the Athletic reported, citing anonymous sources.
The once free-spending Saudi-backed league that turned the golf world upside-down by luring superstars away from the traditional PGA Tour is now expected to have its remaining assets liquidated.

The tour is expected to appear at a Thursday hearing in a bankruptcy court ‌in Trenton, New Jersey, to discuss various contracts, leases and assets. It is unclear whether LIV’s ultimate fate may also be discussed.
Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund had poured an estimated $5bn into the tour since 2022, before abruptly pulling the plug earlier this year.

articles.title: Champions League: Como clobber Lens 9-1 after Real Madrid roar back to deny AEK Athens
articles.summary: Valverde hits late winner as Madrid win 3-2 in Athens. Napoli thrashed by Porto, Club Brugge win at PSV. Anastasios Douvikas led the rout with a hat-trick as Como cruised to a 9-1 victory at Lens, equalling the record for the most goals scored in a single Champions League game.
body: Only two teams had previously won a game by a margin of eight goals since the launch of the modern Champions League in 1992. Liverpool thumped Besiktas 8-0 in the group stage in 2007 and Real Madrid won by the same scoreline against Malmo in 2015.
Como are just the second team to score nine times in a game in the competition, after Bayern Munich beat Dinamo Zagreb 9-2 in the league phase in 2024.
Cesc Fàbregas’s side made it three wins from four in their maiden campaign in the competition with a spellbinding display.

Nico Paz continued his fine form with a goal and two assists, while Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina and Matteo Papaccioli also scored for the Serie A side, who had already beaten both RB Leipzig and Manchester United 4-1 at home in this campaign.
points: Valverde hits late winner as Madrid win 3-2 in Athens.
Anastasios Douvikas led the rout with a hat-trick as Como cruised to a 9-1 victory at Lens, equalling the record for the most goals scored in a single Champions League game.

articles.title: Championship roundup: West Ham stage dramatic comeback on Scott Parker’s opening night
articles.summary: West Ham recover from 3-0 down to draw 3-3 at Cardiff. Leaders Middlesbrough beaten 2-0 at Wrexham. Scott Parker’s return to West Ham had looked like beginning in painful fashion but instead featured a stunning comeback from 3-0 down.
body: Elsewhere in the Championship, the leaders Middlesbrough went down 2-0 at Wrexham.

Parker had been confirmed as West Ham’s head coach earlier on Wednesday, taking over from Nuno Espírito Santo, who was sacked on Tuesday. The club’s former midfielder was appointed on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

A relieved Parker said afterwards: “I came in here at nine o’clock this morning and met the players for the first time, so I didn’t have a lot of input as such. As you can imagine, it was a difficult half-time talk. I just helped them tactically and told them: ‘OK, this is the way it needs to be now.’
“Certainly out of possession, we needed to be more aggressive. There were tactical changes and substitutions, and we became more front-footed. We took a few more risks.”

articles.title: Viktor Gyökeres the difference as Arsenal claim nervy win against Slavia Prague
articles.summary: Another European away day, another victory for Arsenal: albeit only just. This time, Viktor Gyökeres stole the show as poor Slavia Prague matched the longest winless streak in European Cup and Champions League history despite a spirited late comeback.
body: However, had it not been for a wonder save from David Raya, the Czech champions would have snatched a point after Wiktor Nowak pulled one back late on as Mikel Arteta’s usually watertight defence showed signs of fallibility under pressure.
In contrast to last week’s defeat against Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup, Arsenal had been cruising until the last 15 minutes after Noni Madueke fired them ahead early on, set up superbly by Gyökeres.

That was the Sweden striker’s third assist in his past five appearances, although Arteta will have been even more encouraged by the emphatic finish that appeared to put the game beyond Slavia’s reach just before the break.

But the Arsenal manager admitted his side had taken their eye off the ball by allowing their hosts back into the game with some uncharacteristic defensive lapses as Slavia racked up 18 shots to his side’s 12.

articles.title: World record 51 red cards shown in Brazilian youth game
articles.summary: A world record of 43 players and eight members of staff were sent off during an under-20 championship match between Uberlandia and Mamore in Brazil.
body: A world record of 51 red cards were shown during a chaotic under-20s game in Brazil.
The semi-final first leg of the Minas Gerais Under-20 Championship tie between Uberlandia and Mamore was marred by scenes that led to 43 players and eight members of coaching staff being sent off.
The previous record was 36, in a 2011 fifth-division game between Club Atletico Claypole and Victoriano Arenas in Argentina.
Brazilian news outlet O Tempo reported the military police were called, external because of extensive damage to the Parque do Sabia Stadium.

articles.title: 'Sloppy' Arsenal survive second-half scare to beat Slavia Prague
articles.summary: Arsenal survived a second-half fightback from Slavia Prague to win 2-1 at the Fortuna Arena and continue their unbeaten start to the season in the Champions League.
body: The Gunners, runners-up last term, appeared on course for an emphatic victory after scoring twice through Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres in a one-sided first half.
But Slavia roared back into the contest in the second period and gave Arsenal a scare as Wiktor Nowak's late goal from close range set up a nervous finale for Mikel Arteta's side.

Arsenal hung on to claim their third win in four Champions League games but needed a goal-line clearance from Gabriel Magalhaes and several saves from David Raya, who brilliantly pushed an Oskar Kubiak header against the post shortly before Slavia's goal.
Slavia had 17 shots in the second half, having only had one before the break as Arsenal were made to work for a result which looked a foregone conclusion after their dominant start.

articles.title: No end in sight for Russell as he eyes famous All Blacks win
articles.summary: Finn Russell is frustrated at questions about when he might retire as the Scotland fly-half sounds refreshed as he prepares for another attempt to end their hoodoo against the All Blacks.
body: Such is the level of trepidation among Scotland fans as to what life will look like for their team in a post-Finn Russell world, the superstar fly-half has had to field questions for years now as to when he might think about hanging up the boots.
"I'm only 34 – you'd think I'm 44," Russell jokes on the BBC Scotland Rugby Podcast as he prepares for Scotland's Nations Championship showdown with the All Blacks at Murrayfield on Saturday.
"I'm feeling good just now. I think the year after the Lions takes a lot more out of the players than you think - mentally, physically, emotionally.
"It's a big, big high. It's a long season. I think to come back and play the next year as you had done the year before is quite tough.

articles.title: Wolves hit back to beat Bristol City after late Neave double
articles.summary: Substitute Sean Neave scored a late brace as Wolves came from behind to secure a 2-1 Sky Bet Championship win over Bristol City at Ashton Gate.
body: The hosts took a 34th-minute lead when Scott Twine was fouled 25 yards out and got up to fire in an unstoppable right-footed free-kick, sending the ball curling away from Jose Sa's dive and into the top corner.

But Wolves piled on the second-half pressure and were rewarded after 82 minutes when Kieran Trippier volleyed in a cross from the right, Adam Armstrong's first-time shot was saved and Neave pounced to net the rebound.
Six minutes later Neave was on target again, nodding home from close range after Ladislav Krejci had headed a Trippier free-kick across goal.
Wolves were deserved winners and move up to second in the table, but the result was cruel on the Robins, who defended with great tenacity.

articles.title: Boro struggle without Lankshear as Wrexham beat Championship leaders
articles.summary: Championship leaders Middlesbrough suffered only their second league defeat of the season as Wrexham eased the pressure on Phil Parkinson with a much-needed 2-0 win.
body: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Wrexham and Middlesbrough at the Racecourse Ground on Wednesday night; George Thomason and Ollie Rathbone net in home victory.

George Thomason rifled Wrexham in front in the 71st minute and substitute Oli Rathbone sealed it with an 84th-minute header to give Wrexham only their fourth win of the season, coming after back-to-back defeats against Blackburn and Sheffield United left the Red Dragons hovering just above the drop zone.
Boro arrived in Wales unbeaten in 11 league games, but with top scorer Will Lankshear out through injury they looked a far cry from the side who had scored 13 goals in their previous four matches.

Lankshear's return of 15 goals this season was as many as the entire Wrexham squad prior to kick-off, and his absence through injury told on the league leaders as they struggled to make much of an impression before the break.

articles.title: NWSL playoff preview: USWNT stars Trinity Rodman and Sophia Wilson collide - but can anyone stop reigning champions Gotham?
articles.summary: Trinity Rodman meets Sophia Wilson in the first round, and Gotham begins their title defense. GOAL breaks down all eight NWSL playoff teams, key players, and quarterfinal predictions.
body: Gotham FC have a championship to defend and a Shield to go with it. But as the 2026 NWSL playoffs begin this weekend, even a record-breaking regular season offers no guarantees. Eight teams remain, and in two weeks, one will lift the trophy.

It has been a season of breakthroughs and plenty of chaos. Boston Legacy and Denver Summit made an immediate impact in their debut campaigns, the league saw a record number of red cards, and the Utah Royals secured their first playoff berth. The postseason promises another unpredictable chapter.

Ahead of the opening round, GOAL breaks down all eight contenders: how they got here, their key players and potential X factors, and the strengths and weaknesses that could decide their championship chances.

Gotham FC’s title defense begins against a Seattle team that had to fight until Decision Day to secure its place. The No. 1 seed has home-field advantage and a roster packed with international talent, while the Reign arrive with postseason experience and momentum from a strong second half. Seattle has the tools to frustrate the reigning champions, but turning that resistance into an upset will be a tougher challenge.

articles.title: Oxford Utd 2-0 Reading
articles.summary: Substitutes Gatlin O'Donkor and Mo Missanga struck twice in eight minutes to earn Oxford a 2-0 victory over local rivals Reading and a first Thames Valley derby win since 1999.
body: Just minutes after coming off the bench, O'Donkor thundered a low left-footed shot from Cameron Brannagan's free-kick in off the far post to delight the home fans in a packed Kassam Stadium.
After that 71st-minute breakthrough, Missanga then turned in O'Donkor's knock-down at a corner in the 78th minute to seal the three points.
Victory extended the U's unbeaten run to 10 games and lifted Aaron Ramsey's men to third in League One.
Although Reading had their chances, United - who controlled a lot of the possession - deserved the win.

articles.title: Joe Scarborough goes after ESPN’s Pat McAfee: ‘It is a shame for the viewer’
articles.summary: Pat McAfee is a problem for ESPN’s “College GameDay,” Joe Scarborough of “Morning Joe” hammered away at Tuesday during election day. McAfee’s recent headline-grabbing issues with the University of Utah was the tipping point.
body: “I’ve just had enough of this Pat McAfee ruining ‘College GameDay,’” Scarborough said Tuesday. “I look forward to waking up on Saturday mornings and watching that.... It’s like he’s melting down....
“It’s really ESPN. I mean, they run their company the way they want to run their company, but man, it is a shame for the viewer.”
McAfee revealed there have been death threats against him as a result of the controversy surrounding ESPN’s “College GameDay” visit to Utah.

“I’ve stayed away from my mentions and DMs this month since these back to back days but... I’m sure if I went in there now, I’d find some wishes for and threats of death for me,” McAfee posted on X. “‘Don’t read them.’ They’re everywhere.”
